decision: One Claude agent with tools, not many agents
why: Simpler to inspect and test; tools give it exactly the data it needs (profile, role, team, catalog, records, web).
tradeoff: Long tasks run sequentially (~30–60 s per hire).

why: Quotes must exist in the CV; courses, links, mentors and records must be real. Wrong items are sent back once, then corrected.
If Claude is unavailable the service keeps working and labels the plan “Rules”.
tradeoff: Fallback can't catch wrong-person CVs or write warnings.

why: Every step is saved: survives restarts, retries failures, never duplicates invitations.
tradeoff: One server instance (fine for a single company).

why: The agent adapts training and mentoring (reversible); it never decides hiring, probation or pay.
Exercises can't be gamed from the browser; scores are clearly marked as AI-assessed.
tradeoff: No manager sign-off screen (kept the product simple).

decision: Claude Sonnet 5.5 for planning (Haiku 5.5 as a cheaper option)
why: On the held-out set both models scored 100% skill accuracy with zero unsupported claims; Sonnet covered more skill gaps with a course (89% vs 82%).
tradeoff: Sonnet costs ~$0.21 per hire vs ~$0.01 for Haiku — Haiku is a valid choice for high-volume hiring.
